speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing progressive difficulty walking, urinary incontinence, and speech difficulties. To begin my assessment, have you noticed if these symptoms are affecting your legs more than your arms, or if they started in a specific order?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing a gradual difficulty in walking over the past 3 months, requiring wheelchair assistance for the last month. Additionally, there is a history of urinary incontinence for 1 year and recent onset of speech slurring making communication challenging.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: ALS (Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis). The clinical triad of progressive gait disturbance, urinary incontinence, and bulbar symptoms (speech slurring) in a 54-year-old male is highly suggestive of a motor neuron disease affecting both upper and lower motor neurons.
